scenes.name: The Ardent — Deck and Cabin
scenes.description: The Authority's pilot cutter. Cold-open tutorial cabin, Act II's aborted crossing, and the only way to the rock in Act IV.

hotspots.label: Wren's soaked satchel
hotspots.effect: Opens the cold-open conservation puzzle: humidify, separate and blot the two fused leaves of the s.41 commission. Hurrying tears it permanently and scars the document for the rest of the game.

hotspots.label: Conservation roll: spatula, Gore-Tex sheet, blotters
hotspots.effect: Adds the hand-tool kit; unlocks the humidification verb used again on the incinerator fragments in Act I and the razored offsets in Act IV.

hotspots.label: The lee rail
hotspots.effect: Act II aborted crossing: Wren is sick over the side while the beacon comes and goes behind grey water. Her fear of open water as a mechanic, not a line.

hotspots.label: Brass-bound glasses in the locker
hotspots.effect: Act II: at four hundred yards, reveals the beacon's gallery door standing open, contradicting Rita's claim that nobody goes out in the off season.

hotspots.label: The set on its shelf
hotspots.effect: Act V, 07:00: DS Iveson tells Wren an uncautioned confession on a rock is worth precisely nothing. Everything must still be cited.

hotspots.label: Compass and course card
hotspots.effect: Sea travel hub: Rossport Quay, the Brannock slipway, or (Act IV only, with Rita) the Nine Bells landing.

scenes.name: Rossport Quay and the GPO Call Box
scenes.description: The mainland toehold: ferry office, memorial plate, and the red kiosk that is the game's entire hint system.

hotspots.label: GPO call box
hotspots.effect: The diegetic hint line. Phyllida Halkett explains section 41, certification, adverse reports and the 4 November pulping, and refuses every time to have an opinion about the case.

hotspots.label: Ferry office booking book
hotspots.effect: Act IV: H. PIKE, out 08:15, return 17:40 on 14 September 1998. Clears the obvious suspect and implies who worked the counter instead.

hotspots.label: Causeway tide board
hotspots.effect: Posts today's low-water windows; gates travel to Cardew and warns when the causeway is closing.

hotspots.label: Pocketful of ten-pence pieces
hotspots.effect: Limits call length; the pips cut Halkett off mid-procedure unless the player has saved change.

hotspots.label: Cast-iron memorial plate on the harbour wall
hotspots.effect: Thirty-one names, salt-pitted. Cross-referenced against the Pelagia manifest and the Kestrel Bequest schedule in Act IV.

hotspots.label: The bench by the ferry ramp
hotspots.effect: Act IV: Enid Charnock, resigning, unfolds the back cover of the 1974 cash book and hands over the memorandum of 6 November.

scenes.name: Rossport Police Station, Interview Room 2
scenes.description: Two officers and a district of four hundred square miles. The wall the player's case has to be strong enough to stand against.

hotspots.label: DS Marren Iveson
hotspots.effect: Wall-testing dialogue. 'That's an inference, that is. Bring me an object.' Her register changes permanently once handed a properly cited schedule of exhibits.

hotspots.label: Custody record, 31 October 17:15
hotspots.effect: Rita Tain's arrest on Wren's own adverse report. The player reads the consequence of her honesty in a clerk's handwriting.

hotspots.label: Homicide referral form
hotspots.effect: Act V: word the referral from a menu of what can actually be proved. 'Murder' collapses; the grab, the defective rail and the eleven minutes stand.

hotspots.label: Schedule of exhibits
hotspots.effect: Submits the casebook's cited exhibits; each accepted item unlocks a corroborating question Iveson will put on the record.

hotspots.label: Station noticeboard
hotspots.effect: Coastguard bulletins and a storm warning that quietly forecasts the Act IV gale, the downed line and the closed causeway.

scenes.artPrompt: Painterly digital oil painting, 1536x1024, first-person seated view at eye height 1.2 metres across a scratched grey laminate table in a small 1990s police interview room. scenes.ambience: Fluorescent hum, a radio handset squawking down a corridor, a printer, chair legs on vinyl, rain against high glass.

scenes.name: The Slipway and Rita's Shed
scenes.description: Where the Ardent lies and where the causeway starts. Rita's kingdom ashore, and three boxes of a dead man's effects she has never opened.

hotspots.label: The Ardent on her mooring
hotspots.effect: Boards the cutter. Gated by weather: refuses in Act III's southwesterly, permitted only with Rita aboard in the Act IV gale.

hotspots.label: Rita Tain, working on the engine
hotspots.effect: Boat talk, the 1975 findings recited by paragraph number, and the Deakin letter offered in Act II as the thing that ends the case.

hotspots.label: Three unopened boxes of Cormac Sallow's effects
hotspots.effect: Act III: sorting them yields Sallow's file copy of oil requisition R.755, refused, initialled p.p. The object that made him write to a stranger.

hotspots.label: Fog-signal service book on a nail
hotspots.effect: Rita's initials against every month since 1991, catching her claim that nobody goes out to the rock in the off season, and confirming her 14 September alibi.

hotspots.label: Head of the causeway
hotspots.effect: Crosses to Cardew at low water only; the causeway physically closes for hours and, in Act IV, for good.

hotspots.label: The broken davit
hotspots.effect: 1988, and the white scar through Rita's eyebrow. A character note the player finds without being told.

scenes.ambience: Wavelets on concrete, wind in corrugated iron, a halyard tapping, dripping water, distant sheep and gulls.

scenes.name: Cardew Village and the Post Office
scenes.description: One wet street on the mainland side. A dead sorting office, a call box that rang for four minutes in 1974, and the road up to Pike's cottage.

hotspots.label: The call box, Cardew 4471
hotspots.effect: Forty yards from a dead man's door. Standing in it while reading the 1974 plug-log makes the four unanswered minutes physical.

hotspots.label: Cardew sorting office counter
hotspots.effect: The frank die, last struck 30 September 1972: the second nail in the Deakin letter, verifiable against the postmark gazetteer.

hotspots.label: Garage fuel book
hotspots.effect: Act IV: H. Pike, four gallons at 18:20 on 14 September, nine miles from the headland. The alibi he would rather not give.

hotspots.label: The Ship Inn
hotspots.effect: Where Cass Verge was at 22:41 on 3 November 1974 while a telephone rang in the box across the road.

hotspots.label: The pole at the Cardew turn
hotspots.effect: Act IV: taken down by the gale. Cuts the hint line and the police, and forces the Aldis lamp onto the roof.

hotspots.label: The hill road
hotspots.effect: Walks up to Pike's rented cottage; in Act IV the same road is walked toward a fire.

scenes.name: Pike's Cottage, Cardew
scenes.description: Three thousand stolen documents in a rented kitchen, and the table where the reconciliation refuses to agree.

hotspots.label: The kitchen table under the bare bulb
hotspots.effect: THE RECONCILIATION. Dues ledger, oil requisition book and wage sheets filled column by column on a Conservancy form. No hint, no chime; the third column refuses to agree and the music stops.

hotspots.label: Oil Requisition Book, Nine Bells 1966–1980
hotspots.effect: R.741, R.748, R.755, each stamped REQUISITION NOT SANCTIONED — REFER WINTER REFIT, each initialled p.p.

hotspots.label: Despatch Book 1970–79 on the dresser
hotspots.effect: The docket of 16 August 1974 with 74/119 ruled through in 2H pencil and initialled p.p.; foot of the docket, 214 at 4d.

hotspots.label: Catalogue on the backs of tide-table covers
hotspots.effect: Forty years of theft indexed in a chief clerk's hand. Establishes provenance for every exhibit from this house, and the chain-of-custody attack the Board will make.

hotspots.label: Halvard Pike
hotspots.effect: Eleven minutes without stopping, not looking at her: Circular 12/85, the van, and the box marked LIGHTS: STORES he never opened.

hotspots.label: The paraffin heater
hotspots.effect: Foreshadows the Act IV fire, in which the player chooses in smoke which four of nine bundles to carry out.

scenes.ambience: Rain on a kitchen window, a paraffin heater ticking, a mantel clock, paper turning, wind under the door — and at the reconciliation, no music at all.

scenes.name: The Cliff Path and St Bride's Churchyard
scenes.description: The spine of the headland. Thirty-one slate markers along a drystone wall, and the game's weather gauge.

hotspots.label: Thirty-one slate markers along the wall
hotspots.effect: Read individually; names accumulate in the casebook and are matched against the Pelagia manifest and the Kestrel Bequest schedule in Act IV.

hotspots.label: The marker with no dates
hotspots.effect: Emrys Tain, the pilot, buried apart along the wall. The Act V exoneration is measured against this stone.

hotspots.label: Fresh turf, September 1998
hotspots.effect: Cormac Sallow, six weeks in the ground with the flowers gone over. The absent protagonist made physical.

hotspots.label: The headland edge
hotspots.effect: Nine miles out, the dead beacon on its reef: still haze in Act I, storm force 10 in Act IV, hard blue cold on 3 November.

hotspots.label: The lychgate and burial register
hotspots.effect: Thirty-one interments in eleven days of November 1974, in a curate's deteriorating handwriting.

hotspots.label: The path to Pilotage House
hotspots.effect: Returns to the front door or the courtyard side gate; in Act IV the path is under spray and the gate is chained.

scenes.ambience: Steady wind over grass, sea breaking on rock far below, a bell rope knocking, oystercatchers, distant surf.

scenes.name: Brannock House — the Old Sickroom
scenes.description: The Warden's residence along the headland, its 1974 sickroom now a contractor's paint store, with a nurse's ledger still in a box of bills.

hotspots.label: Nurse Kilbride's visit ledger, 1974
hotspots.effect: '12.8.74 — pt. hemiplegic R side, no speech, cannot hold pen, wife present.' Proof of incapacity, source two of three.

hotspots.label: The unfaded rectangle on the wallpaper
hotspots.effect: Where a bed stood for two years. The room's whole history without a word of dialogue.

hotspots.label: Contractor's paint and dust sheets
hotspots.effect: Sandbach's men are using a dead Warden's sickroom as a store; establishes how nearly the ledger was skipped and binned.

hotspots.label: Invalid chair under a sheet
hotspots.effect: A man who could not hold a pen. The physical object behind Link 7 of the proving chain.

hotspots.label: Box of household bills
hotspots.effect: Cross-reference with Dr Munn's locum mileage claims from Accounts to fix 12 August 1974 as the first attendance.

scenes.artPrompt: Painterly digital oil painting, 1536x1024, first-person standing view at eye height 1.6 metres in a stripped upstairs bedroom of a Victorian granite house, now a builders' paint store. Faded rose wallpaper with a clean unfaded rectangle where a bed once stood; stacked paint tins, a folded invalid chair under a dust sheet, a roll of protective board. Key light is thin cool blue-white daylight through a tall sash with peeling white paint, rain on the glass, a grey band of sea beyond. scenes.ambience: Rain on sash glass, a loose window catch, distant hammering, floorboards settling, wind in an empty chimney.

scenes.name: Ottoline's Cottage, 4 Coastguard Row
scenes.description: The warmest room in the game, where a kind woman fetches a biscuit tin down off the dresser and stops digressing.

hotspots.label: The biscuit tin on the dresser
hotspots.effect: Cass Verge's deferment letter of 18 August 1974: residence deferred, wages to continue, you will not discuss this. Initialled p.p.

hotspots.label: Ottoline Verge
hotspots.effect: The break. No accusation; Wren lays out the cards, the stock date, the raised e, the struck-through wage sheets and the tick beside number 29, and Ottoline's sentences go short and flat.

hotspots.label: Photograph on the mantelpiece, 1968
hotspots.effect: Cass Verge in keeper's uniform: the face behind eleven weeks of wages and seven years of drinking.

hotspots.label: Letter from Ilberry naval college
hotspots.effect: Emlyn Verge, second year. The reason a kind woman kept quiet for twenty-four years longer than she needed to.

hotspots.label: The chair by the range
hotspots.effect: A cardigan, a folded handkerchief, a rubber thimble — the same objects as her chair in the Rolls Room, moved eight hundred yards.

scenes.artPrompt: Painterly digital oil painting, 1536x1024, first-person seated view at eye height 1.2 metres in a small warm cottage parlour, evening. A black-leaded range with a low fire, a Welsh dresser crowded with willow-pattern plates and a dented biscuit tin, an armchair with a cardigan over the back. Key light is warm orange firelight from below left plus a soft yellow table lamp with a fringed shade; a small deep-set window shows blue-black rain. Palette: the warmest in the game — amber, madder, brown — against one cold blue window. Mood: safe, kind, and about to be dismantled. No people. No text.
scenes.ambience: Coal settling in a range, a mantel clock, rain at a small window, a kettle just off the boil, wind in the eaves.

scenes.name: The Wicket and Entrance Hall
scenes.description: The building's throat: visitors' book, hook board and the brass head of the pneumatic tube system. Everyone signs in here, including the dead.

hotspots.label: The visitors' book
hotspots.effect: C. SALLOW in at 08:56 on 14 September, never signed out, 'admitted by' initialled S.F-K. Also B. AYLWARD, 6 October, catching his 'I only got here on Tuesday'.

hotspots.label: The hook board
hotspots.effect: Numbered keys by room. The third hook is the strongroom; Pike leaves it there for her in Act III when she has no legal right to it.

hotspots.label: The pneumatic tube head
hotspots.effect: Brass octopus. Sends and receives requisition carriers; in Act II it begins returning the wrong boxes.

hotspots.label: Bram Aylward, 'Ministry liaison'
hotspots.effect: Charming, quick, and lying about exactly one thing. His laser-printed identification card is 1998 paper in a letterpress building.

hotspots.label: Contractor's notice by the door
hotspots.effect: Dated room-closure schedule. Rooms it names genuinely become unavailable on those days.

hotspots.label: Umbrella stand and wet boots
hotspots.effect: Tells the player who is in the building today without a line of dialogue.

scenes.ambience: Flagstone echo, a longcase clock, the thump and hiss of a pneumatic carrier arriving, rain on high glass, a distant door.

scenes.name: The Great Stair and Wardens' Hall
scenes.description: Twenty-two dark portraits of twenty-two men, and the first-floor landing that connects everything above ground level.

hotspots.label: Portrait: Absalom Ferrier, Warden 1961–1976
hotspots.effect: The caption gives the dates of a Wardenship he was unconscious for a quarter of. The player passes it forty times before it means anything.

hotspots.label: Twenty-two Wardens
hotspots.effect: Every one a man, in the same dark ground, back to 1811. Article 9 of the Charter stated as decor rather than dialogue.

hotspots.label: Galvanised ventilation trunk at the landing
hotspots.effect: Forty feet of duct down to the strongroom. In Act II the player hears two women arguing through the other end of it.

hotspots.label: The empty hook at the end of the row
hotspots.effect: No portrait of the current Warden. Nobody has commissioned one and nobody has said why.

hotspots.label: The half-landing window
hotspots.effect: The nine-day weather curve seen from inside: still grey, then streaming glass, then horizontal rain, then hard blue.

hotspots.label: The upper flight
hotspots.effect: Continues to the attic floor: the Chart Loft, the Binding Room and the roof hatch.

scenes.name: The Registry Counter
scenes.description: Where paper is asked for. Slips, stubs, stamps, an Olivetti, and a chief clerk who will not shake your hand.

hotspots.label: Requisition slips and stub book
hotspots.effect: Ottoline teaches the system: white top copy up the tube, pink carbon into the stub, countersignature box, 'if the Warden's out, her clerk initials it p.p.' The twist, taught as housekeeping.

hotspots.label: Standing Order 7, printed on the slip back
hotspots.effect: Every reader's requisition passes the Warden's pigeonhole for countersignature. Read by nobody, and the whole of the Act IV surveillance proof.

hotspots.label: Halvard Pike at the counter
hotspots.effect: Four minutes of unprompted contempt ending on docketing: one hand endorses on the outside third, upside down to the tag. Never journalled, never repeated.

hotspots.label: Olivetti Lettera 32
hotspots.effect: Typewriter survey specimen 3: grey doubling from a slack ribbon vibrator, chipped l.

hotspots.label: Stub book, pink carbons, September 1998
hotspots.effect: Slip R98/2211, 09:10, 14 September, series 14/B box 17, 'issued by' initialled S.F-K. Read in Act I as nothing at all.

hotspots.label: Bundle of treasury tags
hotspots.effect: Pike squares one for her, tail under, loop left, and calls it her people's knot. An object-level fingerprint used in Act IV.

scenes.name: The Long Registry
scenes.description: Six hundred feet of shelving in a single top-lit gallery, and the bound registers that say a notice number was used and then unused.

hotspots.label: Register of Notices Issued, 1974
hotspots.effect: 74/117, 74/118, 74/120. A number used and then unused, with no cancellation minute: the other half of the Act I cliffhanger.

hotspots.label: Bound Rossport Inquiry transcripts
hotspots.effect: Day 9: a Lamp Superintendent answers a question about exhibition with an answer about administration, and a dead pilot pays for it for twenty-four years.

hotspots.label: Ministry staff circulars
hotspots.effect: Lists all four dissolution liaison officers by name. Bram Aylward is not among them.

hotspots.label: Quinquennial Review notice, 22 July 1974
hotspots.effect: An authority found without an effective Warden is to be abolished and its records dispersed. Half the motive, six weeks before the stroke.

hotspots.label: Works orders file
hotspots.effect: Works Order 75/188, June 1975, 'seal chamber, damp', initialled p.p. — the last p.p. anyone ever wrote in this building.

hotspots.label: Shelving stencilled LOT 4
hotspots.effect: State-change marker: bays vanish between acts on the strip-out schedule and their contents become unrequisitionable.

scenes.name: The Strongroom
scenes.description: A barrel-vaulted vault behind a three-movement timelock, where series 14/B sits on the bottom shelf and the door shuts at 18:20.

hotspots.label: Chubb three-movement timelock
hotspots.effect: Set all three movements from the Warden's Order Book closing hours — 1974, 1998 and Saturdays each different. Opens the door, then closes it behind her.

hotspots.label: Japanned deed box stencilled A. FERRIER, WARDEN
hotspots.effect: Empty but for dust, a dead moth and page two of Notice 74/119 on blue-black flimsy: 'until oil supply is restored and the No. 2 vaporiser renewed'.

hotspots.label: Series 14/B box 17
hotspots.effect: Requisitioned 14 September 1998 with no return entry, wearing a new label typed on the Imperial 66 at full 'a' occlusion. A box came home that was never sent home.

hotspots.label: The bottom shelf, 1974
hotspots.effect: The flood: forty minutes of hand-work in the dark, lifting boxes to high shelves by feel with a failing torch. What she saves, she saves.

hotspots.label: Ventilation grille
hotspots.effect: Two women arguing forty feet above. The player transcribes what she is sure of and marks the rest 'not certain'.

hotspots.label: Naismith's Bank letter, 15 August 1974
hotspots.effect: No further facility. Motive in a bank manager's handwriting, four months from insolvency.

scenes.name: The Roof and Signal Mast
scenes.description: Lead walk behind a granite parapet with a signal mast and an Aldis lamp under a tarpaulin. The only way to reach the mainland with the line down.

hotspots.label: Aldis lamp under a tarpaulin
hotspots.effect: The line is down. Look the international code up in the Signal Book, because she does not know it, and signal four miles across black water until Rossport answers.

hotspots.label: The Signal Book
hotspots.effect: Code tables read page by page in the rain. The player composes the message letter by letter and gets it wrong before getting it right.

hotspots.label: The signal mast and halyards
hotspots.effect: Day shapes and storm cones; hoisting the cone is how the coast is told the causeway is shut.

hotspots.label: The parapet
hotspots.effect: The whole map from above: courtyard, churchyard, causeway under six feet of water, and nine miles of black sea with nothing on it.

hotspots.label: Lifted lead flashing
hotspots.effect: Where the rain has been getting into the Long Registry all along. The building dying on its own account, without anyone's help.

scenes.name: The Board Room
scenes.description: The Charter of 1811 in a glazed case, a long mahogany table, and on 3 November the only fully sunlit background in the game.

hotspots.label: The Charter of 1811, Article 9
hotspots.effect: 'The said office of Warden shall be holden by a man of full age.' Never amended in 187 years. The contempt and the alibi in the same clause.

hotspots.label: The case file
hotspots.effect: Act V: eight links — presence, means, opportunity, signature, identity, motive, consciousness of guilt, historical predicate — every assertion tied to an accession number.

hotspots.label: The Board of Dissolution
hotspots.effect: Mrs Ellary Voss, Captain Dunnet and Mr Pargeter for the Ministry, whose job is to strike. Named counter-evidence is fired at every weak link.

hotspots.label: The transcript
hotspots.effect: Uncited assertions are struck aloud, in front of her, and the transcript prints with the gaps in it. Not a fail state; a score.

hotspots.label: The south window
hotspots.effect: At 23:04 on 3 November, three flashes in twenty seconds nine miles out, seen from the room where it was argued.

hotspots.label: The section 41 certificate
hotspots.effect: Signing it saves the archive from the pulper on 4 November, in every ending, whatever else stands or falls.

scenes.name: The Nine Bells — Landing Stage and Doorway
scenes.description: A hundred and twelve feet of granite on a reef, seen from a pitching boat. The jump for the landing is timed to the rise.

hotspots.label: The landing, on the rise
hotspots.effect: Timed to the swell, hands white on the rail, with the Ardent lifting four feet. The cost of the last document, paid in body not file.

hotspots.label: The gallery door far above
hotspots.effect: Standing open at four hundred yards in Act II; from directly beneath, the reason is a broken hasp and twenty-four years of weather.

hotspots.label: The bronze entrance door
hotspots.effect: Sealed since 1974 with a keeper's padlock, whose key is on the third hook nine miles away — which is why it had to be fetched first.

hotspots.label: The Nine Bells reef
hotspots.effect: The rocks the Pelagia struck at 23:04, named on a chart for a hundred and sixty years and seen for the first time from sea level.

hotspots.label: Rita's dry bag
hotspots.effect: What can be carried off the rock and what has to be left. Rita runs for Cardew with the log and leaves the two women behind.

scenes.name: The Nine Bells — Oil Store
scenes.description: The circular base of the tower: empty paraffin drums, a cracked vaporiser on a shelf, and a keeper's log that stops on 24 August 1974.

hotspots.effect: Final entry, 24 August 1974, 22.10: 'No. 2 vapor. cracked. Oil out. Light down. Nothing more to be done here.' The independent record the Authority never held.

hotspots.label: The back of the last page
hotspots.effect: In pencil: tea, boot polish, a birthday card for Nan.

hotspots.effect: The cold smell of a store nobody has opened in twenty-four years, and drum tallies that match the refused requisitions exactly.

hotspots.label: The cracked No. 2 vaporiser
hotspots.effect: On a shelf where somebody put it down. The mechanical fault named on page two of Notice 74/119, in the hand.

hotspots.label: Stores tally board
hotspots.effect: Chalk figures reconcile against the Oil Requisition Book from Pike's cottage, authenticating the refusals against a record outside the Authority's custody.

scenes.name: The Nine Bells — Service Room
scenes.description: A curved whitewashed room with a bunk and a paraffin stove, where two women are shut in for eleven hours and one of them tells the truth.

hotspots.label: The paraffin stove
hotspots.effect: Lighting it is the whole of survival for eleven hours; its blue ring is the only light in the confession.

hotspots.label: Sabine Ferrier-Kyne
hotspots.effect: 04:00: all of it, flatly, in order, with dates, over four hours — and at seven o'clock it is worth precisely nothing.

hotspots.effect: A curved wooden berth with a folded blanket, made up in 1974 by a man who came back for it and was told not to.

hotspots.effect: 07:00: Iveson through four miles of static, telling her to stop crying and go and do her job.

hotspots.label: The stair to the lantern

scenes.name: The Nine Bells — Lantern Room and Gallery
scenes.description: Inside the optic at first light on the anniversary: sector plates, a falling weight, and one Fresnel panel that came home.

hotspots.label: The clockwork Fresnel optic
hotspots.effect: Set the brass occulting sector plates on the rotation drum, wind the weight, set the escapement release for 23:04. Fl(3) W 20s, entered by hand.

hotspots.label: The panel wrapped in a fleece
hotspots.effect: Sandbach bought it back off a shipping agent at four in the morning with money he does not have, and said nothing about it. It goes in here.

hotspots.label: The falling weight and shaft
hotspots.effect: A hundredweight on a chain down the tower's spine; winding it is the last physical act of the game.

hotspots.label: The gallery door
hotspots.effect: Out onto the black gallery rail, a hundred and twelve feet up, where the whole coast is visible and nobody is.

hotspots.label: The lighting-up slate
hotspots.effect: Chalk columns ruled in 1974 and never filled. Wren writes the date on the next line, which is not evidence and is the only thing in the game that is not.
